extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers in neuromorphic hardware design and CMOS circuit designers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and validating CMOS-based neuron and synapse circuits that communicate with time-domain spiking signals, optimized for area and energy efficiency and suitable for reservoir-computing applications. Includes circuit-level design choices, fabrication on a CMOS process, chip measurements, and system-level simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area efficiency (occupied area)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed neuron and synapse occupy the area of 127 μm² and 231 μm², respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller silicon area per neuron/synapse is a key metric for scalability and dense integration. Compare reported area to conventional designs and target reductions relative to op-amp-based implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power / energy efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The design provides higher energy efficiency compared to conventional designs that use operational amplifiers and continuous-time or clocked comparators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize energy consumption per operation/spike. Avoid high-energy building blocks (op-amps, complex comparators); leverage low-power mechanisms (e.g., leakage-driven operation, inverter-based comparators) to reduce overall chip power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal response / time constants
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieves millisecond time constants for temporal signal communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target biologically-relevant (millisecond-scale) time constants when designing neurons/synapses for temporal processing and reservoir computing; validate that circuit time constants meet system-level requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-domain signaling vs voltage/current-domain analog
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of time-domain signals to generate and transmit information, as an alternative to traditional voltage/current-domain analog communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer time-domain signaling when shrinking CMOS device dimensions and lower supply voltages narrow dynamic ranges and reduce noise margins. Time-domain approaches can improve tolerance to limited dynamic range and noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator implementation (inverter-based comparator)
rubrics_metrics.description: An inverter-based comparator is used to realize the firing function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple inverter-based comparators can implement spiking thresholds with lower area and energy than op-amps or complex comparators; evaluate trade-offs in speed, variability, and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leakage-current-driven operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed neural structure is driven by the leakage current of MOS transistors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveraging MOS leakage currents can reduce active power but affects speed and variability; characterize and design around leakage-dependent behaviors to ensure consistent timing and functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabrication / technology node
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabricated using TSMC 65 nm CMOS technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate circuits on a real technology node to validate area, power, and timing claims. Specify the process node since metrics scale with technology choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measured chip validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual chip measurements show that the proposed structure implements the temporal signal communication function with millisecond time constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer measured silicon results over simulation-only claims. Provide measurement data validating target metrics (area, power, time constants, functional correctness) on fabricated chips.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-level demonstration (reservoir computing / learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulation results of the spiking-neural network using the behavioral model of the proposed neural structure demonstrate the learning function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement circuit-level metrics with system-level simulations or experiments (e.g., reservoir computing tasks) to show that components enable intended learning/processing capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of high-energy components / architectural choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional use of op-amps and continuous-time or clocked comparators leads to high energy consumption and large chip area, which is detrimental to building spiking neural networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design architectures that avoid or replace energy- and area-intensive building blocks to improve overall network scalability and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic range and noise immunity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: As CMOS devices shrink and supply voltages decrease, the dynamic range of voltage/current-domain analog circuits becomes narrower and noise immunity decreases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for reduced dynamic range and noise margin in scaled technologies; choose signaling and circuit techniques (e.g., time-domain signaling) that mitigate these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application relevance: suitability for hardware reservoir computing / HCI
rubrics_metrics.description: The implementation of temporal signal communication with millisecond time constants is identified as a critical step toward hardware reservoir computing for human-computer interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess designs for their applicability to target applications (e.g., reservoir computing, HCI), ensuring the circuit metrics (latency, time constants, energy, area) meet application-level constraints.
